correctness.rationale: For each fixed path, departure counts give polynomial dependence on site-law moments; at most 2r departures occur at any site in 4r steps. Reflection and moment matching therefore force static annealed displacement a_n=0 through n=4r. In step 4r+1 the sole possible term containing moment 2r+1 comes from exactly 2r alternating two-step root excursions. The binomial expansion isolates coefficient 2 E[Y^(2r+1)] E[(Y1+Y2)^(2r)], strictly nonzero for nondegenerate asymmetric laws. The geometric-block renewal-reward identity transfers this to the first full-refresh velocity coefficient. Solomon static zero-speed criterion follows from both Jensen bounds E rho>=1 and E rho^(-1)>=1; full refresh is fair. Compact support implies that nonsymmetry yields a first nonzero odd centered moment. Exact rational enumeration independently confirms r=1 and r=2 instances. No finite test is used as proof of general r.

originality.rationale: Martin and Nagel provide a general regenerative speed series, analytic dependence on refresh and the first two full-refresh derivatives. They do not state the all-order positive triangular moment identity or the iff equivalence between law symmetry, identically zero speed and monotonicity in the mean-balanced regime. Their general series is an essential close antecedent and could be used to derive the result, but the full all-rank positivity and symmetry detection require additional path/moment analysis. Deterministic cooling and Solomon results furnish different, credited inputs. No directly equivalent formulation was identified in targeted mathematical searches or accessible previous scientific claims.

value.rationale: Mean site drift one-half makes both static and fully refreshed speeds zero, so the natural question is whether intermediate refreshing can generate transport. The theorem answers this completely: monotone speed exactly characterizes reflection symmetry, while every asymmetric law has induced interior transport. The leading signal is governed by the first odd centered moment at an exactly specified exponent 4r with a strictly positive observable multiplier. The result supplies a natural infinite-hierarchy structural classification, not a one-off computed coefficient.
